findings.evidence: `Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to' (h : ∀ i ∈ s, g i ∈ t) (f : κ → M) : ∑ j ∈ t, ∑ i ∈ s with g i = j, f j = ∑ i ∈ s, f (g i)` (mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/BigOperators/Group/Finset/Basic.lean:272); the existing proof already applies it and then pays `Finset.sum_image hinj.injOn` only to re-index through `C`.
findings.fix: Make the canonical form `∑ σ ∈ T, occCount obs σ • weight σ = ∑ x, weight (obs x)` under `(hT : ∀ x, obs x ∈ T)`, and derive the `columns`-indexed version (via `Finset.sum_image`) and `sum_occCount_eq_card` (`weight := fun _ => 1`) from it.
findings.issue: `sum_occCount_nsmul` states the regrouping identity over an injectively-indexed candidate type `C` (`columns : C → S`, `hinj`, `cover`), which does not match the covering-`Finset` hypothesis style of `sum_occCount_eq_card` at line 80. findings.evidence: Fiber.lean:50-61: the `· rw [occCount_def, Nat.card_eq_zero]; exact Or.inl ⟨fun x ↦ h ⟨x, x.property⟩⟩` branch never uses `hinj`; the statement's `if` is decidable only via the file-local `open scoped Classical`.
findings.fix: Drop the `@[simp]`. Split into an unconditional `occCount_eq_zero_of_forall_ne : (∀ x, obs x ≠ σ) → occCount obs σ = 0` (the `Nat.card_eq_zero` branch, no `hinj` used) and a pattern-restricted `occCount_eq_one_of_injective (hinj) (x : X) : occCount obs (obs x) = 1`, leaving no classical `ite` on any right-hand side.
findings.issue: `@[simp] occCount_of_injective` is a conditional rewrite whose side goal `Function.Injective obs` simp cannot generally discharge, and when it does fire it rewrites `occCount obs σ` into `if ∃ x, obs x = σ then 1 else 0` with a `Classical.propDecidable` instance (from `open scoped Classical in`), which blocks further simplification. It also bundles the zero case, which needs no injectivity.

findings.evidence: Line 91 proves `occCount_eq_sum` by `rw [occCount_eq_card_filter, card_filter]` — no `Fin` content; lines 99-102 and 111-124 use only `card_le_card_of_injOn` / `card_lt_card` on `filter`s over `univ`, so `Fin M ↪ Fin N` can be any `X ↪ Y`.
findings.fix: Move all three into `TauCeti/Data/Fintype/Fiber.lean` in namespace `Function`, generalized to `[Fintype X] [DecidableEq S]` and `e : X ↪ Y`; also remove `Function.occCount` from the `## Main definitions` list at line 39, since it is no longer defined in that file.
findings.issue: Three lemmas about `Function.occCount` remain in namespace `TauCeti` in the word file, `Fin`-specialized, although their statements mention only Mathlib types and their proofs do not touch words: `occCount_eq_sum` (89), `occCount_le_occCount_of_comp_eq` (96), `occCount_lt_occCount_of_comp_eq` (107). The new canonical home therefore has no indicator-sum characterization, and users of `Function.occCount` find its lemmas under `TauCeti.occCount_*`.

findings.evidence: Fiber.lean:28 `Nat.card {x // obs x = σ}` versus Fiber.lean:81 `= Fintype.card X`; `Nat.card_fin` exists at mathlib/Mathlib/SetTheory/Cardinal/Finite.lean:140 for the `Fin` call sites.
findings.fix: State it as `[Finite X] → ∑ σ ∈ T, occCount obs σ = Nat.card X` (the sum is over a `Finset`, so `Finite X` suffices), keeping the file's cardinality convention uniform with the definition.
findings.issue: `sum_occCount_eq_card` requires `[Fintype X]` and concludes `Fintype.card X`, while `occCount` is defined by `Nat.card` (line 28) and its other consumers reason through `occCount_def`. A caller with only `[Finite X]` cannot apply it without inserting `Fintype.ofFinite`.

summary: The relocated `Function.occCount` surface is incomplete in its new home: the indicator-sum characterization and the two monotonicity lemmas stayed in `TauCeti` specialized to `Fin`, the weighted regrouping lemma is stated in an over-fitted injectively-indexed form instead of over a covering `Finset`, and `occCount_of_injective` carries a `@[simp]` that is conditional and produces a classical `ite`.
